sections.h2: Who collects property tax in St. Croix County?
sections.html:
The St. Croix County Treasurer collects property tax for 18 municipalities, takes second-installment and delinquent payments for the whole county, and holds the tax records and assessed values. The office is in the Government Center at 1101 Carmichael Road in Hudson, and the phone number is 715-386-4645.

The treasurer also researches and issues tax deed applications and manages credits. Assessment is a separate job done at the municipal level, so ask your town, village or city clerk who your assessor is. The county's Real Property Listing office (715-386-4680) answers questions about how an owner's name and parcel appear on the tax bill.

The county mails one tax statement per parcel each year to the owner of record. If the deed changes hands after the bills are printed, the county does not mail a new statement, so a buyer may need to ask the treasurer or the local clerk for a copy of the bill.

sections.h2: When are St. Croix County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first installment, or the full payment, is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. Wisconsin bills property tax in arrears, so a bill issued in December 2026 pays for 2026 and is due starting January 31, 2027.

The county says bills arrive in mid-December. Under Wis. Stat. 74.11, a bill under $100 must be paid in full by January 31, and a first installment that is not received within five working days of January 31 makes the whole unpaid balance delinquent on February 1. January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so the statute moves the end of that five-working-day period to the close of business on Friday, February 5. The county's FAQ says payments are timely when received by the due dates, so do not lean on the grace period.

Delinquent taxes in St. Croix County carry interest and penalty of 1.5% per month from February 1, and a fraction of a month counts as a whole month. State law sets interest at 1% per month under Wis. Stat. 74.47, and a county board may add a penalty of up to 0.5% a month. The county offers no payment plans. It encourages owners to pay what they can, and state law allows partial payments of at least $20 on delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: Where do you pay the first installment in St. Croix County?
sections.html:
It depends on the municipality. Some pay the county treasurer from the start, and others collect the first installment locally. The county's payment page lists every one; this excerpt shows the pattern.

MunicipalityWhere to send the first installment
City of Hudson, City of New Richmond, City of River FallsSt. Croix County Treasurer, 1101 Carmichael Rd, Hudson
Villages of Baldwin, Deer Park, Somerset and Star PrairieSt. Croix County Treasurer
Towns of Hudson, Richmond, Somerset, Star Prairie and StantonSt. Croix County Treasurer
City of Glenwood CityCity of Glenwood City Treasurer, 217 West Oak St
Village of North HudsonVillage of North Hudson Treasurer, 400 7th St N
Villages of Hammond, Roberts, Spring Valley, Wilson and WoodvilleThe village treasurer

Source: St. Croix County property tax page. Several towns, such as Baldwin, Cady, Cylon and Emerald, also collect their own first installment. Delinquent payments and second installments go to the county treasurer in every case.

sections.h2: How can you pay a St. Croix County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by mail, in the secure drop box or in person at the Government Center. Online payments go through the county's tax portal, and the vendor charges $1.50 for an e-check and 2.99% for a debit or credit card.

  • By mail: include the parcel number, send the check to the collection location for your municipality, and add a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt.
  • In person: bring the tax information and your payment to the right location, or use the drop box at 1101 Carmichael Road.
  • Online: search the portal by parcel number, address or name, and use only one of those.

The county urges taxpayers to mail payments several days early to avoid postal delay. A tax bill address can be changed with the county's change of address form.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a St. Croix County assessment?
sections.html:
You appeal to your municipality's board of review, not to the county. Under Wis. Stat. 70.47, the board meets once a year during the 45-day period that begins on the fourth Monday of April.

The assessor must mail a notice of a changed assessment at least 15 days before the board meets, or 30 days before in a year of revaluation. Failing to receive the notice does not change the assessment. To object, follow these steps:

  • Tell the board clerk, orally or in writing, at least 48 hours before the first meeting that you intend to object.
  • File a written objection with the clerk within the first two hours of the first meeting, on the form the board requires.
  • State your own estimate of the value of the land and of the improvements, and say what information you used.
  • Present evidence under oath. The board presumes the assessor's value is correct until you rebut it.

An owner of land with a house on it objects to the combined value, not to the land or the house alone. The statute also bars you from testifying if you refused the assessor's written request to view the exterior of the property.

sections.h2: What property tax relief applies in St. Croix County?
sections.html:
The main relief on a house you live in is the state lottery and gaming credit. You qualify if you are a Wisconsin resident who owns the dwelling and uses it as your primary residence on the January 1 certification date. You must apply, and if the credit is missing from your bill you can claim it with your municipal treasurer by January 31 or file a late claim with the Department of Revenue by October 1.

The credit does not apply to rentals, vacant land or garages. When a qualifying house sells, the credit goes with the property, so it should be counted when the buyer and seller prorate taxes. A buyer who will live there files a new application. Ask the St. Croix County Treasurer to confirm whether your parcel is receiving it.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid in St. Croix County?
sections.html:
The county can take the property through a tax deed. The treasurer's page lists a 2026 Notice of Tax Foreclosure, and the county's tax deed page describes how it sells properties it acquires: sealed bids with a 10% deposit, full payment within 30 days of the award, and sale by quit claim deed, as is.

A seller with a delinquent balance has options before it reaches that point. Under Wis. Stat. 74.51, anyone may discharge delinquent taxes before a tax certificate is issued by paying the amount due with interest and any penalty. Under Wis. Stat. 74.53 a county may also sue a person for taxes that were delinquent while that person owned the property, and co-owners are jointly liable. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before you sign a listing agreement.

sections.h2: What is St. Croix County like for a seller?
sections.html:
St. Croix County, with Hudson as its seat, sits on the Minnesota border and is part of the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area. The county was created in 1840 and organized in 1849, and between 2000 and 2010 it was Wisconsin's fastest-growing county. The Census Bureau estimated 98,276 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.1% from April 2020.

From the Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024, the median owner-occupied home is worth $377,700, 78.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, median household income is $103,046, and median gross rent is $1,271. The county issued 460 building permits in 2025, and the average trip to work is 27 minutes. Its four cities are Glenwood City, Hudson, New Richmond and River Falls, the last mostly in Pierce County. New Richmond has a history: an F5 tornado struck it on June 12, 1899.

faqs.q: When is the second installment due in St. Croix County?
faqs.a: July 31. The second installment is paid to the St. Croix County Treasurer, and a payment that is not received within five working days after July 31 makes the entire unpaid balance delinquent on August 1 under Wis. Stat. 74.11(8).

faqs.q: How much interest does St. Croix County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: 1.5% per month from February 1, and a fraction of a month counts as a full month, according to the county treasurer's page. State law sets the base interest at 1% per month, and a county board may add up to 0.5% as a penalty.

faqs.q: Can I make a payment plan with the St. Croix County Treasurer?
faqs.a: No. The treasurer says the office does not set up payment plans. It does encourage owners to make whatever payments they can to cut the balance and the interest. State law accepts partial payments of at least $20 on delinquent taxes.

faqs.q: Who handles a property tax appeal in St. Croix County?
faqs.a: The board of review for your town, village or city handles it. It meets during the 45-day period beginning the fourth Monday of April, and you must give notice at least 48 hours before the first meeting and file a written objection in the first two hours.

faqs.q: Do I get a new tax bill if I buy a St. Croix County house after bills are printed?
faqs.a: No. The county says a change of ownership recorded after the bills are printed does not trigger a new statement. The bill goes to the owner on record, so a buyer should ask the treasurer for a copy.
